contracts.text: The rule must define an error kind with the exact string "action-pinning".
The rule must check step-level action `uses:` references for version pinning.
The rule must check job-level reusable workflow `uses:` references for version pinning.
The rule must be configurable via an `action-pinning` configuration section.
The `action-pinning` config section must accept a `level` field whose valid values are "major-minor", "semver", and "commit-sha".
The default `level` must be "semver" when no explicit level is provided.

Levels must be ordered by increasing strictness: "major-minor" < "semver" < "commit-sha". A ref satisfying a stricter level must also satisfy any less strict requirement (e.g., a commit-sha ref must pass both semver and major-minor checks).
Setting `action-pinning: null` must keep the rule disabled.
An empty object `action-pinning: {}` must enable the rule with default settings.
Local refs (references starting with `./`) must be skipped and not flagged.
Docker refs (references starting with `docker://`) must be skipped and not flagged.
When the action name itself is an expression, the entire `uses:` reference must be skipped entirely with no error reported.
When only the version ref portion is a dynamic expression, the rule must flag it with an error message indicating the ref is a dynamic expression that cannot be verified for pinning.
contracts.adverse_condition: Only the version ref is a dynamic expression, not the entire action name.

contracts.text: The config must support an `allowed-owners` list that is case-insensitive.
The config must support an `allowed-actions` list whose entries use the `owner/repo` format.
The config must support a `denied-owners` list.
The config must support a `denied-actions` list whose entries use the `owner/repo` format.
Global and per-path allowed and denied lists must merge by union across all matching configurations.
contracts.adverse_condition: Multiple configuration sources (global and per-path) both define allowed/denied entries.

contracts.text: Denied entries must take precedence over allowed entries when an entry appears in both lists, but denied entries must still be subject to pinning checks rather than being unconditionally blocked.
contracts.adverse_condition: An entry appears in both the denied list and the allowed list.

contracts.text: For popular actions present in the known-actions data, error suggestions must reference the specific known version (e.g., the pinned version from the known-actions dataset).
contracts.adverse_condition: The action is present in the known-actions data.

contracts.text: Per-path overrides must use an `action-pinning` key to override the pinning level for matching paths.
A per-path `action-pinning` entry must enable the rule for that path even when no global `action-pinning` section exists.
contracts.adverse_condition: No global `action-pinning` config section is present.

contracts.text: An `-action-pinning-level` CLI flag must be accepted, overriding only the pinning level (not allow/deny lists).
The `-action-pinning-level` CLI flag must enable the rule even when it would otherwise be disabled (e.g., via `action-pinning: null` or absence of config).
contracts.adverse_condition: The rule is disabled via config (null or absent).

contracts.text: Config validation must reject invalid `level` values (anything other than "major-minor", "semver", or "commit-sha").
contracts.adverse_condition: A config or override specifies a level not in the allowed set.

contracts.text: Config validation must reject owner entries in `allowed-owners` or `denied-owners` that contain a slash (`/`).
contracts.adverse_condition: An owner entry contains a slash character.

contracts.text: Config validation must reject malformed entries in `allowed-actions` or `denied-actions` that do not match the `owner/repo` format.
contracts.adverse_condition: An action entry does not follow the `owner/repo` format.

contracts.text: Error messages for reusable workflow `uses:` violations must be distinguishable from error messages for step action `uses:` violations.
All work must be done on a new branch created from main and committed when complete.
